local_meaning.text: Dangerous winds on the water. Boats should be back on their moorings or hauled; check your lines and fenders now. Expect scattered power outages from limbs on lines; charge your phone while you can.

Expect damaging wind, coastal flooding, and multi-day power outages. Haul boats or double all lines now. If officials suggest leaving low-lying areas, do it early. Fill water jugs; wells need electric pumps.
Water may cover low sections of shore roads and docks, especially near high tide. Move cars, gear, and anything floatable above the shoreline before the peak. Don't drive through water on the road.
Gusts can drop limbs onto power lines, so outages are possible. Secure trash cans, deck furniture, and anything that can blow into a line or a window. Take extra care in a high-sided vehicle.
Plows reach side roads slowly, so plan to stay put. Stock up before it starts, keep the fuel tank full, and locate your shovel now. If you rely on medical equipment, arrange backup power today.

Ice is a common cause of multi-day outages. Charge everything, fill water jugs, and plan for warmth without power. Never heat with a gas stove or grill indoors. Stay off the roads until they are treated.
Brief but violent wind and lightning. Get off the water and out of the yard. Unplug sensitive electronics.
Go to the lowest floor, an interior room, away from windows, now. A basement beats any room with glass.
Never drive through water on a road; two feet of water floats a car. Culverts can wash out; report road damage to the town office.
Near-zero visibility on the water and on the roads. Delay boat trips; use low beams and slow way down.
Check on older neighbors without air conditioning, mornings and evenings. Drink water steadily. Find a public place to cool off.
Conditions are rough for skiffs, kayaks, and small boats. If you don't have to go out, don't. If you do, file a float plan with someone on shore and wear the life jacket.
Stay off wet rocks and ledges facing open water; waves arrive in sets, and the big one comes without warning. Keep a close eye on children near the shore.
